headlines.title: Digital Power ICs - Global Strategic Business Report: Data Centers' Appetite for Power Drives Digital Power Chips Toward $103 Billion
headlines.summary: The global digital power IC market is projected to nearly double from $54.9 billion in 2024 to $103 billion by 2030, a new Research and Markets report finds, as 5G networks, EVs and efficiency rules lift demand for chips from Texas Instruments, Infineon, Analog Devices and NXP.Dublin, Oct. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- "Digital Power ICs - Global Strategic Business Report" has been added to ResearchAndMarkets.com's offering.

headlines.title: Texas Instruments: 3 Things to Watch Before Buying the Dividend Stock
headlines.summary: Texas Instruments Incorporated (NASDAQ:TXN) stands out as a favorite among long-term dividend investors. The company’s analog chips and embedded processors power everything from industrial machines and cars to data centers and home electronics.

headlines.title: Sandisk (SNDK)  vs. Texas Instruments (TXN): How Much Cash-Yield Protection Does Memory Offer?
headlines.summary: Our 10 Best Semiconductor Stocks to Buy for the Next Decade includes both memory and analog exposure. Sandisk’s strong cash generation creates an apparent valuation advantage over Texas Instruments. The useful question is how much that cash can decline before the advantage disappears, rather than assuming today’s memory economics last a decade.

headlines.title: These 3 Chip Giants Turn Massive Cash Flow Into Growing Dividends
headlines.summary: Most income investors write off chipmakers the moment they see the yield, but a handful of semiconductor companies have been quietly compounding their payouts through recessions, factory buildouts, and market downturns in ways that reframe what a dividend stock can look like.

headlines.title: Broadcom (AVGO) vs. Texas Instruments (TXN): Higher Income or Stronger Dividend Coverage?
headlines.summary: Our 10 Best Semiconductor Stocks to Buy for the Next Decade ranks durable franchises using weighted sentiment, business resilience and valuation. Two names raise a separate income question: how much can shareholders collect without relying on an uninterrupted boom? Broadcom Inc. (NASDAQ:AVGO) has stronger recent dividend coverage. Texas Instruments Incorporated (NASDAQ:TXN) pays the higher yield.

description: Texas Instruments Incorporated designs, manufactures, and sells semiconductors to electronics designers and manufacturers in the United States, China, the rest of Asia, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, Japan, and internationally. It operates through Analog and Embedded Processing segments. The Analog segment offers power products to manage power requirements across various voltage levels, including battery-management solutions, DC/DC switching regulators, AC/DC and isolated controllers and converters, power switches, linear regulators, voltage references, multiphase controllers and power stages, and lighting products. This segment also provides signal chain products that sense, condition, and measure real-world signals and convert them into data to be transferred or converted for further processing and control, such as amplifiers, data converters, interface products, motor drives, clocks, and logic and sensing products. The Embedded Processing segment offers microcontrollers, processors, wireless connectivity, and radar products; and applications processors for specific computing activity. It also provides DLP products primarily for use in projecting high-definition images; calculators; and application-specific integrated circuits. Its products are used in various markets, such as industrial, automotive, personal electronics, communications equipment, enterprise systems, calculators, and others. The company markets and sells its semiconductor products through direct sales and distributors, as well as through its website. Texas Instruments Incorporated was founded in 1930 and is headquartered in Dallas, Texas.
